chunks: And from him, from al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥaḍramī, from Samā‘ah, who said:

I asked him about forgetfulness in the morning prayer. He said: “If you do not know whether you prayed one rak‘ah or two, then repeat the prayer from its beginning. And the Friday prayer as well: if the Imam forgets in it, then he must repeat the prayer, because it is two rak‘ahs. And the maghrib prayer: if forgetfulness occurs in it and he does not know how many rak‘ahs he prayed, then he must repeat the prayer.”

key_terms.أَنْ يُعِيدَ الصَّلَاةَ: that he must repeat the prayer
key_terms.السَّهْوِ: forgetfulness or inadvertent doubt occurring during prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts the number of rak‘ahs in fajr, jumu‘ah, or maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on doubt caused by forgetfulness in certain prayers. It states that if uncertainty occurs in the two-rak‘ah morning prayer, the Friday prayer, or the maghrib prayer in a way that leaves the number of rak‘ahs unknown, the prayer must be repeated.
